rule: Approval attaches to results, not to tasks. Work is filed without asking; only acting on it is gated, and only by how hard it is to walk back.

0.name: Just do it
0.means: Nothing to walk back — reading, drafting, analysing, rendering, running the suites.
0.gate: none; the result is what he reviews

1.name: Do it, show the diff
1.means: Changes files, but git reverts it — doc edits, code behind tests, a new decision card.
1.gate: a build session does it and shows the diff afterwards

2.name: Ask first
2.means: Hard to walk back or his taste to settle — shipping, spending, deleting, anything players see, any change of design direction.

consider: A question from Daniel, or anything he asks the studio to consider, look into, weigh, or think about, is tier-0 work: reading, analysing and recommending, which nobody needs permission for. File the consideration, owned by whoever holds the answer, with a first step that produces a recommendation. Never file the action he is asking about as if he had asked for it — that is filed later, at its own tier, when he accepts the recommendation.
comment: A comment on a card is not a verdict and needs no button. Its owner answers it on the card and makes one of three moves, named on the card: answer (the reply settles it), revise (the owner extends the existing result and it comes back for review), or follow-up (new work filed to the right person, linked to the card).
